blocks.raw: # Retro guide
blocks.text: Retro guide

blocks.raw: This page provides you with information on transactions that are applied/added to a loyalty program after the transaction has taken place.
blocks.text: This page provides you with information on transactions that are applied/added to a loyalty program after the transaction has taken place.

blocks.raw: Retroactive transactions, also known as retro transactions, refer to transactions that are applied/added to a loyalty program after the transaction has taken place.
blocks.text: Retroactive transactions, also known as retro transactions, refer to transactions that are applied/added to a loyalty program after the transaction has taken place.

blocks.raw: This is a common scenario in many domains and can occur for a variety of reasons:
blocks.text: This is a common scenario in many domains and can occur for a variety of reasons:

blocks.raw:
* An error in the transaction process
* A delay in the transaction being recorded
* The customer has not provided the loyalty details at the time of the transaction
blocks.text: An error in the transaction processA delay in the transaction being recordedThe customer has not provided the loyalty details at the time of the transaction

blocks.raw: ## Air lines example:
blocks.text: Air lines example:

blocks.raw: Generally in airlines, sometimes customer won’t provide their loyalty details at the time of the transaction. So basically that becomes a non-loyalty transaction, and because of that, no loyalty benefits will be given to that customer.
blocks.text: Generally in airlines, sometimes customer won’t provide their loyalty details at the time of the transaction. So basically that becomes a non-loyalty transaction, and because of that, no loyalty benefits will be given to that customer.

blocks.raw: However, the same customer will call customer service sometime in the future, and request to convert that non-loyalty transaction in the past to a loyalty transaction. Upon validating a few details, generally, most airlines will agree to that. This is a case of a retro transaction.
blocks.text: However, the same customer will call customer service sometime in the future, and request to convert that non-loyalty transaction in the past to a loyalty transaction. Upon validating a few details, generally, most airlines will agree to that. This is a case of a retro transaction.

blocks.raw: ## Primary requisite to use retro functionality:
blocks.text: Primary requisite to use retro functionality:

blocks.raw: Whenever a brand wants to utilize this retro transaction functionality, they have to raise a ticket with the sustenance team to configure a setting from the backend.
blocks.text: Whenever a brand wants to utilize this retro transaction functionality, they have to raise a ticket with the sustenance team to configure a setting from the backend.

blocks.raw: ## Scenarios of retro processing:
blocks.text: Scenarios of retro processing:

blocks.raw: There are primarily two ways in which the retro processing will happen:
blocks.text: There are primarily two ways in which the retro processing will happen:

blocks.raw:
1. Workflow rules-based retro processing (point in time program and promotion configurations)
2. Tier-based retro processing (point in time tier of the customer)
blocks.text: Workflow rules-based retro processing (point in time program and promotion configurations)Tier-based retro processing (point in time tier of the customer)

blocks.raw: ### Workflow rules-based retro processing:
blocks.text: Workflow rules-based retro processing:

blocks.raw: Let’s understand with the help of a real-case scenario. There is a customer who made a ‘non-loyalty’ transaction on 20th May 2023.
blocks.text: Let’s understand with the help of a real-case scenario. There is a customer who made a ‘non-loyalty’ transaction on 20th May 2023.

blocks.raw: However, the same customer called the customer service on 17th August 2023 requesting to convert that ‘non-loyalty’ transaction to a ‘loyalty transaction’.
blocks.text: However, the same customer called the customer service on 17th August 2023 requesting to convert that ‘non-loyalty’ transaction to a ‘loyalty transaction’.

blocks.raw: In this case, had the brand already enabled ‘retro-transaction’, then the processing of that transaction should happen according to the workflow rules set on 20th May 2023.

1. On 20th May 2023, say the rules present in the workflow are ‘XYZ’.
2. On 10th August 2023, say the brand has changed those rules to ‘ABC’.

To avoid this, always create new set whenever you are replacing the rules in your workflows.

**Important callout**\

blocks.raw: ### Tier-based retro processing:
blocks.text: Tier-based retro processing:

blocks.raw: Similar to the above case, let’s say this time, the action is not simple points allocation, but rather some kind of setting depending on the tier of the customer.
blocks.text: Similar to the above case, let’s say this time, the action is not simple points allocation, but rather some kind of setting depending on the tier of the customer.

blocks.raw:
* Gold tier: 20% of the transaction amount
* Silver tier: 15% of the transaction amount
* Bronze tier: 10% of the transaction amount
blocks.text: Gold tier: 20% of the transaction amountSilver tier: 15% of the transaction amountBronze tier: 10% of the transaction amount
